research_metadata.project_title: Minimum-Cost Emergency Communication Network Using Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)
research_metadata.course_context: Discrete Mathematics and Graph Theory (DMGT) Experiential Learning Project
research_metadata.benchmark_fuel_source: Government of Karnataka Finance Department Notification (effective June 15, 2024, raising sales tax on diesel from 14.34% to 18.44%, yielding ₹88.94/L in Bengaluru; petrol revised to ₹102.86/L at 29.84%)

verified_official_statutory_rates.issuing_authority: Government of Karnataka, Department of Health & Family Welfare / Transport Department
verified_official_statutory_rates.document_title: Notification on Maximum Fare Ceiling for Private Ambulance Services
verified_official_statutory_rates.order_identifier: State Government Directives under Karnataka Epidemic Diseases Ordinance / Act, 2020
verified_official_statutory_rates.statutory_type: Government Order / Regulated Maximum Consumer Tariff Cap
verified_official_statutory_rates.target_service: Private Commercial Ambulance Operators (Patient Transport & Basic Life Support)
cost_components_included: Commercial operator overhead and profit margin
verified_official_statutory_rates.regulatory_notes: Statutory ceiling enforced to prevent private operator price-gouging during public health emergencies. Because the signed government gazette circular PDF is not accessible via open-access portal, this figure is classified as secondary-source reported. It does NOT represent the marginal per-kilometer running cost of operating a state-owned emergency fleet vehicle.

ambulance_108_arogya_kavacha.agency: National Health Mission (NHM) Karnataka / Directorate of Health & Family Welfare Services
ambulance_108_arogya_kavacha.reason: The Karnataka State Government directly funds 108 Arogya Kavacha through departmental budget lines (bulk fuel procurement, institutional maintenance contracts, and salaried staff payroll) rather than reimbursing an official statutory per-km operating fee. No Gazette notification prescribes an internal per-km fleet expenditure figure.

police_patrol_hoysala.agency: Karnataka Police Motor Transport (KPMT) Wing / Bengaluru City Police
police_patrol_hoysala.reason: Police Hoysala patrol vehicles are maintained via departmental police garages and state fuel allocations. There is no public tariff or official per-km charge in police regulations.

fire_engine_ksfes.agency: Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services (KSFES)
fire_engine_ksfes.reason: Firefighting is a non-commercial state emergency function funded through state budget allocations. KSFES tenders specify chassis procurement and pump equipment standards rather than a per-km operating expenditure tariff.

illustrative_derived_estimates.label: Illustrative Estimate — Not an Official or Verified Operating Rate
illustrative_derived_estimates.disclaimer: These values are engineering approximations derived for academic modeling purposes to simulate emergency response logistics. They are not official statutory government rates. Specific inputs for fuel efficiency and routine maintenance are unsupported engineering assumptions.
illustrative_derived_estimates.methodology: Direct Operating Cost = (Diesel Retail Price / Fuel Efficiency) + Estimated Routine Fleet Maintenance Provision

unsupported_inputs_disclosure.fuel_efficiency_km_l: Representative OEM baseline estimates under urban stop-and-go driving conditions; not audited departmental fuel logs.
unsupported_inputs_disclosure.maintenance_provision_inr_per_km: Estimated allowance for periodic servicing, lubricants, filters, and tire amortisation; not derived from official state garage balance sheets.

ambulance.representative_chassis: Force Motors Traveller 3350 / Tata Winger 2.2L CRDe Diesel

diesel_price_sensitivity.condition: ±15% Retail Diesel (₹75.60 to ₹102.28 / L), holding efficiency (10.0 km/L) and maintenance (₹3.61/km) constant

fuel_efficiency_sensitivity.condition: Varying efficiency from 11.0 km/L (cruising) to 9.0 km/L (congestion), holding diesel price (₹88.94/L) and maintenance constant

maintenance_sensitivity.condition: ±25% Maintenance provision (₹2.70 to ₹4.51 / km), holding diesel price and efficiency constant

combined_operating_scenarios.condition: Combined Best Case (cruising highway, lower wear) vs Base vs Worst Case (severe congestion, high wear)

police_patrol.representative_chassis: Mahindra Bolero B6 / Maruti Suzuki Ertiga 1.5L Diesel

diesel_price_sensitivity.condition: ±15% Retail Diesel (₹75.60 to ₹102.28 / L), holding efficiency (12.0 km/L) and maintenance (₹2.59/km) constant

fuel_efficiency_sensitivity.condition: Varying efficiency from 13.5 km/L (highway patrol) to 10.5 km/L (dense city patrol)

combined_operating_scenarios.condition: Combined Best Case (cruising highway patrol) vs Worst Case (congested city patrol)

fire_engine.representative_chassis: Ashok Leyland 1618 / Tata 1613 16-Tonne GVW (4,500L Water Tanker, PTO Centrifugal Pump)

diesel_price_sensitivity.condition: ±15% Retail Diesel (₹75.60 to ₹102.28 / L), holding efficiency (2.8 km/L) and maintenance (₹10.24/km) constant

fuel_efficiency_sensitivity.condition: Varying efficiency from 3.5 km/L (ring road cruising) to 2.2 km/L (heavy idling / PTO pump operation)

combined_operating_scenarios.condition: Combined Best Case (open corridor transit) vs Worst Case (severe urban delay and pumping)

unsupported_claims_rejected.claim: The ₹120.00/km ambulance tariff is the government fleet operating expenditure.
unsupported_claims_rejected.justification: The ₹120.00/km rate is a consumer price ceiling reported in secondary media coverage citing a May 2021 order by the Karnataka Department of Health & Family Welfare to cap private commercial ambulance charges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Conflating a private consumer charge with direct internal government fleet mechanical operating expenditure is mathematically and administratively incorrect.

unsupported_claims_rejected.claim: ₹12.50/km, ₹10.00/km, and ₹42.00/km are statutory rates published in the Karnataka Government Gazette.
unsupported_claims_rejected.justification: No Karnataka Government Gazette order publishes these per-kilometer operating figures. They are engineering estimates derived from fuel economy and diesel benchmark prices, and must strictly be presented as illustrative derived estimates with explicit disclosure of unsupported efficiency/maintenance assumptions.

unsupported_claims_rejected.claim: Emergency response arrival time is the sum of travel times of all responding agencies.
unsupported_claims_rejected.justification: All responding agencies are alerted and dispatched concurrently upon incident confirmation. The time to secure the scene is governed by the latest arriving vehicle (max T_j), not the physical fallacy of summing concurrent durations (sum T_j).

unsupported_claims_rejected.claim: The MST edges represent physically installed telecommunication cables connecting facilities.
unsupported_claims_rejected.justification: The MST is a conceptual mathematical communication-backbone model minimizing theoretical interconnectivity distance using straight-line geodesic Haversine edge weights. It does not represent physically trenched fiber-optic or wired telecommunication infrastructure.
